newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Cathay eyes third U.S. gateway.
newsitem.headline: Cathay eyes third U.S. gateway.

text.p: HONG KONG, May 1( Reuter) - Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd said it is studying a third U.S. gateway following the March signing of a new air services agreement between Hong Kong and the U.S.

The airline's deputy managing director Philip Chen said the new American gateway could be one of 14 new cities which the agreement allows Cathay to fly to without a limit on frequencies, but he declined to identify which airports are being evaluated.
The former head of Hong Kong Dragon Airlines (Dragonair)was speaking to journalists for the first time since taking over the senior Cathay position in February.
Cathay currently operates both passengers and cargo flights to New York and Los Angeles.
Industry observers said Chicago is a prime candidate taking advantage of Chicago O'Hare's huge hubbing operations within the U.S. marketplace.
Cathay has already announced it is to take over from its 75 percent subsiiary and all-cargo airline Air Hong Kong and restart Boeing 747-400 freighter services to Chicago later this year.

"This agreement will allow us tremendous new opportunities. We have to undertake a good study to understand what the market is like, what is the potential and how do we use it. This study is at the very initial stages at the moment," Chen said.

Chen said it was unlikely any new U.S. routes would be started until after the opening of Hong Kong's new airport at Chek Lap Kok, due in 12 months' time, because of slot restrictions at the existing congested Kai Tak airport.

"A new service may start before Chep Lap Kok but not in a very big way because if we want to start a new daily service, we would have to ask for 14 slots at Kai Tak. Tell me, where we would get those?" Chen added.

When asked about potential alliances with a U.S. partner, and previously reported prelimiary talks with United Airlines, Chen said Cathay was always open to suggestions but declined additional comment.
